items.title: Five Marks to Take Up Against Five Deep Delusions, and Five Approaches That Bring the Mind to Liberation

items.zh: 又有五種能圓滿解脫、厭離所對治法。謂於諸法中，有三種愚以為依止，起三顛倒。三種愚者，一、時節愚，二、分位愚，三、自性愚。三顛倒者，一、於無常計常顛倒，二者、於苦計樂顛倒，三、於無我計我顛倒。及規求利養、希望壽命。為治如是五所治法，起五取相。謂於諸行，取無常相，亦取苦相；於諸法中，取無我相；於飲食中、取惡逆相；於其命根，取中夭相。又有五種修定修智二勝行者正心解脫生長之門。定勝行者，因聞依諦聖言論故，正解法義。如因聽聞，因廣大音讀誦經典，因為他人開闡妙義，在空閑處審諦思惟，正解法義，當知亦爾。智勝行者，於上品亂貪欲對治無倒思惟。
items.en: There are also five things that bring full liberation from and disenchantment with what is to be counteracted. Namely, with respect to phenomena, there are three kinds of delusion serving as a basis, giving rise to three inversions. The three delusions: delusion regarding time, delusion regarding condition, delusion regarding intrinsic nature. The three inversions: taking the impermanent as permanent, taking suffering as pleasant, taking the selfless as a self. And also: scheming for material support, and longing for a long life. To counteract these five things, five marks are taken up: with respect to formations, taking up the mark of impermanence and the mark of suffering; with respect to phenomena, taking up the mark of selflessness; with respect to food, taking up the mark of repulsiveness; with respect to the life-faculty, taking up the mark of a life cut short. There are also five doorways by which one who excels in both cultivating concentration and cultivating wisdom brings about and grows the liberation of mind. The excellent practice of concentration: through hearing discourse grounded in the noble truths, correctly understanding the teaching's meaning; as through hearing, so too through reciting scripture aloud, through expounding its profound meaning for others, and through careful reflection in solitude — know it is likewise so. The excellent practice of wisdom: undistorted reflection that counteracts the coarsest, most disordered craving.

items.title: Aspiration and Method Both Fully Present, and the Five Feelings That Trouble Body and Mind Alike

items.zh: 又有五種修觀行者意樂方便悉皆具足。謂於涅槃、菩提、起猛利信解，名意樂具足。無間殷重修習正智而行、奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，名方便具足。又有五法，令諸有情受愛非愛業果異熟，煩惱身心，具攝眾苦。謂苦、樂、憂、喜、捨。又由成就如前所說意樂方便悉皆具足不退轉故，令觀行者堪能速證聖諦現觀，亦善安住諸勝善品。
items.en: There are also five things by which one who cultivates contemplation has aspiration and method both fully present: giving rise to fierce confidence and resolve towards nirvāṇa and enlightenment is called aspiration fully present. Cultivating, without interruption and with earnest care, correct knowledge in conduct, calm, and insight, is called method fully present. By accomplishing this aspiration and method, both fully present and unwavering, one who contemplates becomes capable of swiftly realising direct insight into the noble truths, and of skilfully abiding in every excellent, wholesome quality. There are also five things that cause sentient beings to experience the ripened fruit of agreeable and disagreeable karma, troubling body and mind, comprehending the whole of suffering: pain, pleasure, grief, joy, and equanimity.

items.title: Five Ways a Non-Returner Reaches Final Nirvāṇa, and Five Grades of the Pure Abodes Reached Through Mixed Cultivation

items.zh: 又有五種離欲界欲未盡餘結學生差別。一、住中有，便能究竟得般涅槃。二、於初靜慮初受生已，得般涅槃。三、受生已後，少用功力聖道現前，得般涅槃。四、多用功力聖道現前，得般涅槃。五、或色界邊際乃至色究竟，得般涅槃；或無色界邊際乃至有頂，方能究竟得般涅槃。又有五種雜修第四靜慮果得不還者生地差別。一、下品靜慮果生地，二、中品靜慮果生地，三、上品靜慮果生地，四、上勝品靜慮果生地，五、上極品靜慮果生地。
items.en: There are also five distinctions among trainees, free of desire for the desire realm but with remaining fetters not yet exhausted, regarding how rebirth occurs: first, dwelling in the intermediate state, one is thereby able to reach final nirvāṇa; second, having just been reborn in the first dhyāna, one reaches nirvāṇa; third, having been reborn, with little exertion the noble path manifests and one reaches nirvāṇa; fourth, with much exertion the noble path manifests and one reaches nirvāṇa; fifth, one reaches nirvāṇa only at the very limit of the form realm, up through its highest heaven, or only at the very limit of the formless realm, up through the peak of existence. There are also five distinctions in the ground of rebirth for a non-returner who attains the fruit of mixed cultivation of the fourth dhyāna: the ground reached by an inferior grade, a middling grade, a superior grade, a superior-excelling grade, and a superior-ultimate grade of that same cultivation.

items.title: An Arhat Tested Against Every Provocation at Once — "Five Things" Closes

items.zh: 又有五種修觀行者觀察作意，能令三界煩惱永斷究竟決定。謂雖深厚憶念分別思惟欲相，於諸欲中仍不趣入。任運捨心，於離欲相率爾思惟，便能任運其心趣入。如於欲離欲相，如是於恚無恚相，害無害相、色等至生相、無色等至生相，及涅槃相，當知亦爾。
items.en: There are also five observational attentions of one who cultivates contemplation, capable of permanently severing the afflictions of the three realms, bringing this to ultimate and settled certainty. Namely: although one deliberately, deeply calls to mind and reflects on the mark of desire, the mind still does not enter into any of the desires; equanimity operates spontaneously, and simply by reflecting, however casually, on the mark of freedom from desire, the mind spontaneously enters into it. As with the mark of desire and freedom from desire, know it is likewise so with the mark of hostility and freedom from hostility, of cruelty and freedom from cruelty, of the attainments and rebirths of the form and formless realms, and of the mark of nirvāṇa itself.

items.title: The Sixth Numeric Category Opens: Eight Facets of a Being's Experience, Each Multiplied by Six

items.zh: 已說五種佛教所應知處。次說六種。謂依六相，宣說八種有情事差別。為令墮在我及有情、命者見等眾生，趣入無我故。謂我所依事差別、境界事差別、自性事差別、受用因事差別、受用事差別、隨說事差別、作用事差別、希望事差別。
items.en: The five-thing category of what a Buddhist should know has now been explained. Next, the six-thing category. By way of six aspects, eight distinct matters concerning sentient beings are expounded, in order to bring beings who have fallen into the views of self, of a sentient being, of a life-possessor, and the like, into selflessness. Namely: the matter of what the self depends on, the matter of its objects, the matter of its own nature, the matter of the cause of its enjoyment, the matter of its enjoyment itself, the matter of what is spoken accordingly, the matter of its function, and the matter of its longing.

items.zh: 於如是等事差別中，未善純熟修觀行者，便謂有我。依眼等根；於色等境；由觸及受種種受用；有如是名、如是種、如是姓、如是食等於自於他隨起言說；造作一切法非法行；於可愛事希望和合、久住、增益、於非愛事悕望不合、不住損減。若於如是事差別中，已善純熟修觀行者，爾時妄計皆不得生。
items.en: Within these distinctions of matters, one who has not yet become well practised in contemplation thinks there is a self: one that relies on the eye and other faculties; that, towards forms and other objects, experiences them in various ways through contact and feeling; about which, for oneself and others, people speak of 'such a name, such a kind, such a family, such food' and so on; that performs all dharmic and non-dharmic deeds; and that, in regard to what is pleasant, hopes for union, long duration, and increase, and in regard to what is unpleasant, hopes for no union, no duration, and decrease. When one has become well practised in contemplation within these distinctions of matters, none of these false notions can arise.

items.title: Six Kinds of Disrespect That Erode All Wholesome Progress, and Where Craving, Hostility, and Delusion Each Take Root

items.zh: 又於寶學有六輕懱，能令善法或未得退，或已得退，捨佛聖教，乃至微信亦皆退失。謂於佛法僧寶，增上戒學、增上心學、增上慧學。由惡友故，於增上心、慧令得邪僻教誡教授；由惡語故，全無所得。彼由邪僻及無所得故，退失一切所有善法。與此相違，當知即是白品六法。又有情心與不如理作意俱行，於色等境有六種貪所依處平等分位。如貪所依處平等分位，如是瞋所依處不平等分位，癡所依處非平等非不平等分位，當知亦爾。
items.en: There are also six kinds of disrespect towards the jewels and the trainings, capable of causing wholesome qualities not yet attained to remain unattained, or already attained to be lost, forsaking the Buddha's sacred teaching down to the last trace of faith: namely, towards the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha jewels, and towards the higher training in precepts, concentration, and wisdom. Through evil companions, one comes to receive distorted instruction regarding the higher mind and wisdom; through evil words, one gains nothing at all. Because of this distortion and this gaining nothing, one loses every wholesome quality one has. Further, when a sentient being's mind operates together with incorrect attention, there are six loci on which craving depends with respect to form and the other sense-objects, in the state where they accord with one's mind. As with craving's locus in the state of accord, know it is likewise so with hostility's locus in the state of discord, and delusion's locus in the state of neither accord nor discord.

blocks.text: Today completes the fives and opens the sixes. One passage gives an unexpected way to deepen understanding: explaining the teaching to others.

Three delusions give rise to inversions (Day 3). The *Pīxún jì*: not knowing formations across time is the delusion that gives rise to permanence; not knowing feelings, the delusion that gives rise to pleasure; and so on. Each inversion has a root in a specific ignorance.

The mind is brought to liberation through five approaches; one is "through another's exposition". Venerable Miào Jìng reads the Chinese the other way round: "because you expound the profound meaning of the four truths for others", and in explaining, you understand more deeply. Every teacher knows this: one learns a text best by teaching it.
Five things make aspiration and method complete. Venerable Miào Jìng: faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom, the five faculties; calm and insight are concentration and wisdom.

subs.head: Five non-returners; five grades of pure abodes

blocks.text: A non-returner reaches final nirvāṇa in five ways (in the intermediate state, upon rebirth, with effort, without effort, and by going upstream). The five pure abodes come from five grades of mixed cultivation (Day 24). Venerable Miào Jìng works out the counts: the highest grade alternates fifteen moments, five contaminated and ten uncontaminated.

An arhat is tested against every provocation at once: the form and formless attainments, even the mark of nirvāṇa, are all surpassed. Venerable Miào Jìng: the four dhyānas surpass desire, the formless attainments surpass form, and nirvāṇa surpasses all.

subs.head: The sixes: eight facets of experience, each sixfold

blocks.text: A being's experience has eight facets (faculties, objects, consciousnesses, contacts, feelings, perceptions, intentions, cravings), each sixfold by sense. The *Pīxún jì* gives the details. What is "spoken accordingly" about a being: name, kind (caste), lineage, food, and lifespan.

Six kinds of disrespect erode wholesome progress: towards the Buddha, Dharma, Saṅgha, trainings, and so on. The *Pīxún jì*: "because of not revering the Buddha and Saṅgha, one relies on evil friends and receives distorted teaching." Disrespect comes first; bad company follows. Venerable Miào Jìng on where craving takes root: in objects that "accord with my mind", that go along with my wishes.

quiz.q: Three delusions give rise to three inversions. How does the Pixunji pair them?
options: all three give rise to the self-inversion
delusion of time gives the self-inversion, of nature the permanence-inversion
ignorance of formations across time is delusion of time, giving permanence; of feelings is delusion of condition, giving pleasure; of the nature of phenomena is delusion of nature, giving self
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: not knowing formations across the prior limit and so on is delusion of time, hence the permanence-inversion; not knowing feelings is delusion of condition, hence the pleasure-inversion; not knowing the nature of phenomena is delusion of nature, hence the self-inversion.

quiz.q: The English renders 因為他人開闡妙義 as "through another's exposition." How do the lectures read it?
options: one expounds the profound meaning for others, and in teaching understands it more deeply — the opposite of the English
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: because you expound and explain in detail the profound meaning of the four truths for others, you come to understand it deeply — teaching and learning grow together. Master Cháng Bǎi agrees. The English reverses the direction.

quiz.q: The treatise lists five things — aspiration and method fully present. What five does Venerable Miào Jìng identify them with?
options: faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom — calm and insight being concentration and wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Calm and insight below are concentration and wisdom; faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom — these are the five methods." Master Cháng Bǎi credits this five-faculty mapping to him: the two resolves are faith, unbroken earnestness is diligence.

quiz.q: The five grades of mixed cultivation culminate in fifteen attentions. How does Venerable Miào Jìng count them, and where does the reading note go wrong?
options: cumulative counts of 3, 6, 9, 12, 15; the top grade's fifteen = five contaminated plus ten uncontaminated; the note says a triad repeated six to fifteen times
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Five are contaminated attentions and ten uncontaminated; together, fifteen." The previous grade had twelve; this adds three. This "interleaved perfuming" sandwiches contaminated attention between uncontaminated ones; without it, no rebirth in the Pure Abodes.

quiz.q: Eight matters are expounded "by way of six aspects." What are the six, per the Pixunji?
options: each of the eight has six: six faculties, objects, consciousnesses, contacts, feelings, perceptions, intentions, cravings
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "In each one there are six aspects: six faculties, six objects, six consciousnesses, six contacts, six feelings, six perceptions, six intentions, six cravings — in that order." Master Cháng Bǎi: grasping the consciousnesses as self is the matter of its own nature.

quiz.q: What causal direction does the Pixunji give between the six disrespects and evil friends and words, and what does the reading note say?
options: the Pixunji: first disrespect towards Buddha and Saṅgha, then reliance on evil friends; disrespect towards Dharma, then evil teaching; the note reverses this
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "Because of not revering the Buddha and Saṅgha, one relies on evil friends and receives distorted instruction; and because of not revering the true Dharma, one hears wrongly taught doctrine — this is evil words." Disrespect comes first.

quiz.q: The English renders 平等分位 as "in equal measure." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say 平等 means?
options: the object accords with my mind — going along with my wishes and liking — that is "equal"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "平等 means according with my mind — it goes along with my wishes; I like it, and it goes along with my liking." The *Pixunji*: pleasant feeling arising from an agreeable object is the "equal" state. "In equal measure" misses this.
